1. Dockerfile.serving's new demo stage breaks every EXISTING caller that builds with no --target at all. Docker's default (no --target) always builds the LAST stage declared in the Dockerfile textually. demo must be declared with FROM runtime AS demo (it builds on top of runtime), so it is necessarily textually AFTER runtime - meaning it is now the last stage, and the implicit default silently became demo instead of runtime. Proof: tests/test_container_build.py::test_a_real_docker_build_of_the_serving_image_succeeds and tests/test_serving_dependency_lock.py::test_a_real_docker_build_of_the_serving_image_can_still_import_the_server both run a plain docker build -f Dockerfile.serving -t ... . with no --target, and both now fail: docker tries to pull demo-data from Docker Hub as a real image/registry repo (since no --build-context demo-data=... was supplied, exactly as any caller not opting into the demo stage would not supply one) and gets pull access denied, repository does not exist. Dockerfile.serving's own new comment block claims the default docker build with no --target still produces exactly the runtime stage above, byte-for-byte - this claim is FALSE as shipped; it was never actually verified against a plain default build, only against explicit --target runtime (docker-compose.yml) and explicit --target demo (manual testing). Fix: add ONE trailing anonymous stage directly after the demo stage's two lines, so the Dockerfile's own LAST stage textually is byte-identical to runtime again:

   FROM runtime AS demo
   COPY --from=demo-data --chown=foss-mcp:foss-mcp . /data/manifests

   # Re-anchors the Dockerfile's own last stage back to runtime's exact content. Docker's
   # default target (no --target) is always the LAST stage declared textually, and demo must
   # be declared after runtime (it builds FROM it) - so without this trailing stage, a plain
   # docker build with no --target would silently build demo instead of runtime. This
   # stage adds no instructions of its own, so it is byte-identical to runtime.
   FROM runtime
